description: Find the lexicographically greatest nonincreasing four-square representation of one bounded integer.

source.title: Express number as sum of four squares
source.reference: Codewars kata title used as discovery input only
source.mathematical_reference: Pollack and Treviño, Finding the Four Squares in Lagrange's Theorem
source.algorithm_attribution: Bounded descending coordinate enumeration with exact square checks

output.encoding: four nonincreasing components packed as base-33 digits: (((a*33)+b)*33+c)*33+d

contract.decomposition: Return the lexicographically greatest tuple (a,b,c,d) with 32>=a>=b>=c>=d>=0 and N=a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2.
contract.canonical_order: Among all nonincreasing nonnegative representations, maximize a, then b, then c, then d.
contract.result_decoding: Read four base-33 digits from most significant to least significant to recover a,b,c,d.
contract.no_solution_note: Unreachable for valid N by Lagrange's four-square theorem.

complexity.independent_time: O(N) pair construction plus bounded pair-sum lookup

workspace.meaning: Primary uses scalar loop state only.
